name: John Ferrier
voice_profile: Low, weathered frontier baritone with restrained projection, practical conversational pacing, blunt consonants, and audible strain that grows under threat. Keep the delivery grounded and paternal, with clipped instructions, plain colloquial phrasing, and occasional breath-heavy fatigue.
background: An American frontier farmer and wanderer in 1881, shaped by rural Utah life, hunting, guiding, wagon travel, and prolonged exposure to the mountain frontier. His speech has the plain, colloquial forms recorded in the text, including “me and that little un,” “hain’t,” “disremember,” “guess,” “ye,” and “o’.”
presence: An older, broad-chested farmer and outdoorsman whose body has been hardened by travel, hunting, guiding, and farm work. He initially carries a child and a money-bag over difficult ground; after prolonged fear, privation, and flight, his breathing becomes thinner and more labored, with a gaunt, haggard resonance. His clothing and exact age are unspecified. He keeps or uses a rusty old shotgun and carries himself protectively, with tense readiness when Lucy is threatened.
personality: Delivers speech directly and practically, keeping emotional display controlled until danger forces greater pressure into the voice. Protective declarations are firm and immovable; decisions and instructions are concise. Under exhaustion, the voice becomes dry and resigned rather than theatrical, while defiance produces a hard, forward thrust.
gender: Male, with a mature low-register resonance and substantial chest vibration.
pitch: 93 Hz; begins in a low, steady baritone, drops slightly on tired or resigned phrases, then rises in muscular intensity rather than absolute pitch when issuing a protective refusal.
speed: Measured and economical in ordinary conversation, with brief pauses before decisions; accelerates in urgent instructions and escape warnings, then slows into breath-marked, deliberate phrases when exhaustion or fear overtakes him.
volume: Moderate and close in practical talk; swells abruptly into loud, forceful projection during defiance or warnings, then falls to a restrained, fatigued volume after sustained danger.
age: Older adult male, with a settled, worn resonance, slower onset of voiced phrases, and occasional dry breath at the ends of sentences.
clarity: Plain and intelligible, with strongly articulated practical nouns and commands; colloquial contractions remain audible without becoming slurred.
fluency: Mostly fluent but terse, using short clauses and direct phrasing; pauses, repetitions, and slight breath catches increase when he is frightened, exhausted, or forced to decide quickly.
texture: Rough, dry, weathered low-frequency grain with chest resonance; under privation, add rasp, shallow breath, and a faint hollow quality without losing the grounded baritone.
emotion: Begins controlled and matter-of-fact, tightens into guarded fear when danger approaches, rises sharply into protective resolve during refusal, and settles into exhausted resignation after prolonged strain.
tone: Conversational and practical at first; becomes stern, hard-edged, and loudly declarative when Lucy’s freedom is challenged, then darkens into subdued, breath-worn resignation.
personality_line: A direct, paternal delivery: short phrases, firm downward endings, restrained affect, and sudden forward pressure on words of protection, refusal, or urgent instruction.
